slides.title: Title Slide: Understanding Tokens and Tokenization
slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on Understanding **Tokens** and **Tokenization**.
slides.image_prompt: Title slide with 'Understanding Tokens and Tokenization' and EduPyramids logo.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to explain what **tokens** are.
You will understand how **tokenization** works.
And why **tokens** are crucial for **LLM** performance and cost.
slides.image_prompt: Learning objectives slide with bullet points for token explanation, tokenization process, and importance for LLM performance and cost.

slides.title: Prerequisites
slides.narration:
To follow this tutorial, learners should have basic knowledge of using the internet.
And what **LLMs** are.
slides.image_prompt: Prerequisites slide listing basic internet knowledge and understanding of LLMs.

slides.title: How LLMs Understand Text
slides.narration:
**LLMs** don't read words like we do.
Instead, they read **tokens**.
This is a fundamental concept.
slides.image_prompt: An abstract illustration showing text being broken down into smaller, numbered units, representing tokens, with an LLM icon processing them.

slides.title: What is a Tokenizer?
content: It splits raw text into sub-word pieces.
These are the **tokens** the model understands.
slides.narration:
So, what are these **tokens**?
A **Tokenizer** is like a special dictionary.
It splits raw text.
It breaks it into smaller, sub-word pieces.
These are the **tokens** that the **LLM** understands.
slides.image_prompt: An icon representing a dictionary or a translator, showing text input and then output as smaller, distinct blocks labelled 'tokens'.

slides.title: Token Examples
slides.narration:
Let's look at some examples.
A simple word like "The" might be just one **token**.
But a complex word like "**Tokenization**" might be broken down.
It could become three **tokens**: **Token**, **iz**, **ation**.
slides.image_prompt: Visual example: 'The' -> [The]. 'Tokenization' -> [Token], [iz], [ation]. Show text splitting into colored blocks.

slides.title: Why Do Tokens Matter?
slides.narration:
Now, why should you care about **tokens**?
Understanding them is very important.
It directly impacts how you use **LLMs**.
It also affects the cost of using them.
slides.image_prompt: A question mark icon surrounded by small token-like shapes, with arrows pointing to icons representing 'cost' and 'performance'.

slides.title: Tokens and Context Windows
content: It sets a hard limit on input size.
slides.narration:
First, consider **Context Windows**.
This is an **LLM**'s 'short-term memory'.
Its size is measured in a fixed number of **tokens**.
This sets a hard limit.
slides.image_prompt: An illustration of a window frame with small token shapes flowing into it, and a scale measuring the number of tokens, implying a limit.

slides.title: Context Window Limits
content: This limits your **prompt** and document size.
It's the maximum 'context' you can send.
slides.narration:
For example, some **LLMs** have a limit of 8,192 **tokens**.
This means your **prompt** and retrieved documents cannot exceed this.
It is the maximum 'context' you can send at once.
slides.image_prompt: A visual representation of a fixed-size 'context window' filling up with text snippets and a user's prompt, showing a 'max token' counter.

slides.title: Tokens and Cost
slides.narration:
Next, let's talk about cost.
**API** providers charge you per **token**.
So, using fewer **tokens** directly reduces your expenses.
Efficiency can dramatically save you money.
slides.image_prompt: A coin or money icon next to a stack of tokens, with an arrow pointing to a calculator or a decreasing cost graph.

slides.title: RAG and Token Efficiency
slides.narration:
An efficient **RAG** system uses fewer **tokens**.
Consider **GraphRAG**.
It can reduce **tokens** needed by 26% to 97%.
This makes running your **AI** applications much cheaper.
slides.image_prompt: A visual comparing two paths, one with many small tokens and another with fewer tokens, representing efficient RAG systems like GraphRAG, with a cost reduction percentage shown.

slides.title: Tokens and Document Chunking
content: When we '**chunk**' documents, we split them.
slides.narration:
Finally, **tokens** are vital for **chunking**.
When we '**chunk**' our documents, we split them.
This prepares them for the **LLM**.
**Token** count helps us manage these chunks effectively.
slides.image_prompt: An illustration showing a long document being broken into smaller, manageable 'chunks', with each chunk having a token count label.

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
With this, we come to the end of this tutorial.
Let us summarise.
We learned that **LLMs** process text using **tokens**.
**Tokenizers** break text into these **tokens**.
And understanding **tokens** is key for **context window** limits, **API** costs, and efficient **chunking**.
slides.image_prompt: Summary slide with key takeaways about tokens, tokenizers, context windows, API costs, and chunking.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
As an assignment, please do the following.
Find an online **Tokenizer** tool.
Experiment with different sentences.
Observe how words are broken into **tokens**.
Pay attention to how punctuation and spaces are handled.
